cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Approve the Harmless Version
cards.instruction: Get approval for a harmless version of your plan, then gradually reveal what that approval now commits them to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll organise Sunday. All right if my aunt and uncle come for tea?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I'll make tea for two.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Their three children are coming too; I'll squeeze them onto the bench.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll buy the cake. You only have to make the tea you agreed to; I'll keep the extra cups washed.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 organises and seeks small approval, A3 expands the party and A5 takes extra jobs to preserve B service.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 explicitly promises tea for two; A3 adds three and B4 refuses baking; A5 substitutes bought cake and additional washing.

relationship.evidence: B2 limited labour and B4 workload concern are consistent; A5 responds with actual work rather than a label.

heightening.evidence: A5 insists the original tea promise still covers the expanded visit, softened by B4 prompted concessions.

specificity.evidence: A1 two adults and A3 three children make B4 five guests arithmetically coherent.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 cake, tea and cups each answer the practical conflict without explaining the card title.
